subject: HealthLytics bake-off: recap, open tests, and proposed plan of action
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@healthlytics.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HealthLytics bake-off: recap, open tests, and proposed plan of action

Hi Alyssa / Daniel —

Thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we have a clear plan for the bake-off. I pulled the highlights from the call and added a few probing items we should validate during the PoC.

Pain points you reiterated:
- Inconsistent 95/99p latency on current inference stack during bursts (real‑time triage use case).
- Unit cost is creeping up with current long‑context workflows (4–8k tokens).
- Regulatory requirement: PHI must remain within a customer VPC / no redaction allowed — strong need for private deployment option.
- Need for deterministic fallbacks when high‑priority requests fail (graceful degradation).

Goals you shared:
1) <1) 99p latency under 200ms for 2k avg request size across production mix.>
2) Predictable monthly unit costs with visibility per‑route and token band; want <20% reduction vs current supplier> as a stretch.
3) SOC2 evidence and audit log access for external audits.
4) Clear SSO + SCIM onboarding for engineers and shared access controls.

Decision criteria we proposed to align on this week:
- Latency SLOs: 99p and median targets across short (<=512), medium (512–2k), and long (2k–8k) contexts.
- Cost: token unit economics and delta from current vendor under realistic traffic profile.
- Security: VPC/private deployment feasibility, KMS integrations, and evidence for SOC2 controls.
- Quality: model output parity on your 10 canonical prompts and safety/PII handling.

Open tests we recommend for the bake-off (I included owners / timelines):
1) Tail latency run: 24‑hour simulated traffic (50RPS burst windows) — owner: Dylan — target: by 2026‑08‑14.
2) Long‑context accuracy and KV cache validation on 10 canonical prompts (compare Redwood vs incumbent) — owner: Marissa — target: by 2026‑08‑16.
3) VPC/Private deployment smoke test (data flows, audit logs, KMS key rotation) — owner: Karthik (infra) — target: by 2026‑08‑20.
4) Cost modeling exercise: token mix + batching profiles for your workload — owner: Dylan/Finance — target: initial estimate by 2026‑08‑13.

Attachments: I attached a short discovery notes PDF and a proposed PoC workbook that maps each test to success criteria.

Next steps (concrete):
- Alyssa / Daniel: confirm the canonical prompts list (can paste in reply) and pick 2–3 SLA metrics you want prioritized.
- I’ll schedule the tail latency run and share a lightweight traffic script and dashboard link.
- Karthik will reach out to your infra team to kickoff the VPC checklist and scoping call.

If that all looks good I’ll lock the PoC plan and send a calendar invite for the kickoff next Tuesday.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

—
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Email: dylan@redwood.com | Mobile: +1 (415) 555‑0124
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@healthlytics.com>

Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthLytics bake-off: recap, open tests, and proposed plan of action

Dylan —

Thanks for the crisp summary. This aligns with our expectations. A few clarifications from our side before you spin up the tests: 

1) For the tail latency run — can you scope the burst profile as 100RPS for 2‑minute windows (we see short spikes during ingest)?
2) On cost modeling: please include both quantized and FP16 runs so we can see the delta.
3) For the VPC smoke test — we need a short list of required IAM roles and an approximate maintenance window (1–2 hours ok).

Canonical prompts: (paste below — these are the 10 we want in the PoC)
- PHI redaction check: "Summarize the intake notes while preserving identifying info for clinician review."
- Triage classification: "Prioritize the messages for urgent follow‑ups."
- SOAP note extraction: "Extract HPI, Rx, and plan sections into structured fields."
- 7 more prompts attached in a doc (see drive link).

We approve the proposed dates broadly. Please loop in your infra/solutions owner for the VPC kickoff — Daniel will coordinate timing on our side (he’s copied).

—
Alyssa Chen
Director of Clinical Data Platforms | HealthLytics
alyssa.chen@healthlytics.com

Thanks Alyssa — perfect. Quick confirmations: 
- Tail latency burst adjusted to 100RPS 2‑minute windows (we’ll simulate your traffic mix).
- Cost modeling will include quantized vs FP16 and a sensitivity table for request size distribution.
- Karthik will send the VPC checklist and IAM role template by EOD; we’ll propose a 2‑hour maintenance window early morning.

I’m attaching the PoC workbook with the test matrix and acceptance criteria (HLT-proposed-poc-plan.xlsx). Also attaching my quick discovery notes.

I’ll schedule the kickoff for Tue 2026‑08‑11 10:00am PT — sending invite pending confirmation from Daniel.

On the quality test: Marissa will own the canonical prompt comparison and will return a short evaluation report with examples and scoring (pass/flag/reject).

Looping internally with a quick checklist so we don’t drop anything: 
- Dylan: tail latency + cost model (due 8/13).
- Marissa: canonical prompts eval and flagging report (due 8/16).
- Karthik: VPC checklist + contact infra lead (target 8/20).
- Ops: prepare trace hooks and token-level billing for the PoC (I’ll escalate to infra ops).

Notes: be mindful of PHI constraints — no external logging without explicit redaction rules. If the VPC path will take longer, we should prepare a fallback canary using a dedicated tenant with strict data retention for the first pass.

I’ll join the kickoff on 8/11 and will bring a short rubric for pass/fail on model outputs.
